questions.explanation: Expectation weights each value by its probability: E(X) = 0(0.2) + 1(0.5) + 2(0.3) = 0 + 0.5 + 0.6 = 1.1. It is the balance point of the distribution, not a value X ever takes.
questions.prompt: A discrete random variable X takes values 0, 1, 2 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3. What is E(X)?

questions.answer: 0.3. The probabilities in a discrete distribution sum to 1, so P(X = 2) = 1 - 0.2 - 0.5 = 0.3.
questions.explanation: Every discrete probability distribution sums to exactly 1 because something has to happen: 1 - 0.2 - 0.5 = 0.3. Checking the sum first also catches invalid tables before any further work.
questions.prompt: A probability table for X lists P(X = 0) = 0.2 and P(X = 1) = 0.5, with X = 2 the only other outcome. Find P(X = 2) and state the rule you used.

questions.explanation: Choose which 3 of the 10 trials succeed - 120 ways - then multiply by the probability of one such path: 3 successes at 0.3 each and 7 failures at 0.7 each. The product is about 0.267, roughly a 1-in-4 chance.
questions.prompt: Let X be the number of successes in 10 independent trials, each with success probability 0.3. Write down the formula for P(X = 3) and evaluate it.
